bridges.description: Show that physical resurrection best explains Christianity's origins without claiming deductive necessity.
Establish that the Gospels and Acts preserve substantially trustworthy, close-to-events testimony.
Argue that the reported encounters resist honest mistake and that costly proclamation supports sincerity.
Argue that religious context and the purpose of signs keep resurrection from an automatically disqualifying prior probability.
Challenge resurrection's comparative superiority and favor a natural explanation of Christian origins.
Argue that oral development, literary dependence, historical kernels and elaboration can explain the texts without eyewitness authorship.
Keep a sincere-mistake origin live and question whether named witnesses' precise claims and risks are independently established.
Argue that testimony alone does not overcome the lower prior probability assigned to a miracle while allowing stronger documentation to matter.
